UniStartJena App
UniStartJena is the official study start app of the University of Jena. The app provides you with all the important information: enrolment, your first semester, your study programme, push notifications, interactive map, FAQ. Available in all app stores, free.
Image: Christoph Worsch (University of Jena)
Most frequently asked, urgent questions
What is the status of my application?
Please check the status in our
application portal
External link
.
Is my enrolment completed with the application for enrolment?
No, please read "Application for enrolment" in the chapter
Enrolment
and follow all steps.
When should I transfer my semester fee?
Please make the transfer only if your timely arrival in Jena (visa) is sure. See the chapter
Enrolment
.
Which health insurance should I mention in my application for enrolment?
If you have not got a German statutory health insurance yet, please enter no data. Please see more on this in #2 in the chapter
Before Arrival
and in the chapter
Enrolment
.
Has my application for enrolment been received?
Please check the status in our
application portal
External link
.
Can I enroll (pay the semester fee) or study online or from outside Germany?
Yes, but please pay only if your timely arrival (visa) is sure. Make sure the correct amount is transferred and the correct reference is used. Please read all about deadlines in the
Enrolment
chapter below.
Can I get an enrolment certificate for my visa application?
Please use your admission letter for the visa application. An
enrolment certificate
is issued only after enrolment has been completed, see the enrolment steps
below
.
Which official contact person should I mention in my visa application?
Dr. Britta Salheiser, Internationales Büro der Universität Jena, Fürstengraben 1, 07743 Jena,
incoming@uni-jena.de
, +49 (0)3641 9-401521.
What should I do if my visa is granted late?
Please read the first subchapter in
Enrolment
. In case you cannot make it to Jena by 30 October 2026 (winter semester 2026) at the latest, you should not enroll, because this will lead to severe problems later in your studies.
Is there a scholarship for me and how can I apply?
Scholarships are not automatically provided with admission. You have to apply for a scholarship between 6-12 months before it starts. Please read all about financing your studies in #4 in the chapter
Before Arrival
.
I don't have a room yet. What should I do?
Please search on the private market, in the cities near Jena. For more information, see the chapter
Before Arrival
.
How do I get a Welcome Buddy to help me?
Please see the information in the chapter
Before Arrival
.
Do I need a blocked account?
All degree-seeking students from outside the EU will need a blocked account, see the details in the chapter
Living in Jena
.
Can I enroll without a permanent address in Germany?
Yes, the University accepts a temporary Germany address for enrollment and does not need the official registration certificate. So if you live in a hostel or with friends, please provide this address. For the registration at the Residents Registration Office/Citizens Service you will need a certificate (Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung) from your regular, permanent accommodation provider. Registration should be made within 14 days after moving in (or at the next appointment available). See the details in the chapter
Living in Jena
.
How do I get a semester ticket?
After completing your enrolment, you will get your semester ticket (see the
After enrolment
chapter)  (valid from 1 April/1 October); until then please buy local transport tickets, e.g. the
VMT
External link
weekly ticket. The
Deutschlandticket
External link
may be cheaper than a monthly or regional ticket, but remember to cancel it by 10 April/October.
Learn more
Where can I print documents?
If you (or friends) have got a thoska with credit on it, you may use the copy machines on campus or in the Computer Centre. Otherwise, take a USB drive (or send an email) to any of the copy shops (at Krautgasse, Schlossgasse, Unter der Kirche). Coin-operated copiers are located on level 0 in the main library building (Bibliotheksplatz 2) and in the Law, Economics and Social Sciences sub-library (Carl-Zeiss-Straße 3). Maybe a friend has got a printer?
How can I pay at the canteen without my thoska?
See the information about the
thoska
in the
After enrolment
chapter.
Where can I leave my bags after arrival?
Baggage lockers can be found at the
Paradies station
External link
.
Will anybody pick me up at the airport?
Jena does not offer this service. Please us the information about
Travelling to Jena
below to plan your journey.
I need to withdraw from enrolment, what do I do?
Please contact the International Office at
incoming@uni-jena.de
.
How can I get in contact with other students?
In the chapter "
Welcome on Campus
" we give you some suggestions.

Status "Request for enrolment" = your application has not yet arrived
Status "Application for enrolment in progress" = your application has arrived, is being processed like many others, you might still have to take the next steps 2-4 below
Info "missing documents" = your application is not complete, see details in the portal
Status "Enrolled" = your application is complete and you have gained students status. Please read messages in the portal and your emails.
Please
do not inquire by email after the status of your application; this will only slow up processing all applications.
Visa
Visa necessary?
First, please check with the help of the
Foreign Office portal
External link
if you need an entry visa if you want to study in Germany. Do not enter with a tourist/Schengen visa, because this is not valid for studying and cannot be changed into a student residence permit.
Citizens of a few countries (non-EU) may enter Germany visa-free, but still must register their residential adress and apply for a residence permit after arrival (see
Living in Jena
).
If you already have a residence title, e.g. for au pair or work, please clarify 5 months before the start of your studies with the responsible Immigration Office whether you can continue your studies at the University of Jena directly afterwards or whether you have to leave Germany beforehand and apply for a visa from abroad.
Your passport should be valid at least 6 more months.
Visa application
Make an appointment as early as possible. Please use your
admission letter
to apply for a student visa
as soon as you receive it
. Apply for your
visa for studying or seeking a university place
at the
Consular Services Portal
External link
of the German Foreign Office. Please note:
You need to upload your passport, admission letter, proof of financial ressources, health insurance, language certificates, motivation letter.
Applications are processed in the order of registration. Processing may take between 2-12 months.
We do not provide enrolment certificates until after enrolment has ben finished (see
below
). An information about the required language level can be quoted from the
study programme description
.
If you are required to provide a
university contact person
in the visa application, please mention:
Dr. Britta Salheiser, Internationales Büro der Universität Jena, Fürstengraben 1, 07743 Jena,
incoming@uni-jena.de
, +49 (0)3641 9-401521.
FAQ
External link
Proof of financial ressources
You should set aside approx. EUR 750-900/month to cover rent, health insurance, food, books, and personal items (
overview of living costs
pdf, 1 mb
· de
). A semster fee breakdown is given in the invoice after applying for enrolment in the Friedolin portal.
Applying for a student visa or residence permit, students should be able to prove sufficient financial means of EURO 11,904 or EURO 13,092 in the DSH course (2026) for the first year in a
blocked account
External link
. Please see our information about blocked accounts in our website on
financing your studies
.
Health insurance
Applying for a student visa, you will have to show a health insurance for travel to Germany. You can freely choose this health insurance for the trip, but please also note the information provided by the German embassy.
For the enrolment other rules apply, see
below
. Some of the insurance providers mentioned there also offer travel insurances which are valid for visa applications.
Coming to Jena from another German university or changing your study programme:
It may be that your current visa is valid for the studies at your old university only (see the green paper in addition to your visa card) or for your old study programme. Complete your enrolment by 15 February/August and apply for your new residence permit right away.
Changing the University:
In this case, you must apply for a new student visa after enrolling at the University of Jena. If you live and study in another city/university in German,
1. deregister at the other university (apply as soon as possible, termination date 30.9./31.3.).
2. apply for
enrolment
at the University of Jena.
3. move to the Jena region, register your address at the
City Registration Office.
4. apply for a new residence permit at the local
Immigration Office
.
Previously enrolled as a
visiting student at another German university
as part of an exchange programme with a university in another EU country, you must first leave Germany, apply for a student visa at an embassy outside Germany and then re-enter.
Change of study programme
(e.g. from guest studies or DSH course to regular studies, or change of subject): In the case of such a change, it is not always possible to stay without leaving Germany and re-applying for a visa. Please inform your local Immigration Office (Ausländerbehörde) about your plans before you make the change. Please note that changes from the DSH course to the Master's course or from the Master's course to the Bachelor's course will not be approved without detailed justification.
After enrolment
Visas are usually valid for 12 months (guest students: planned duration of stay). Please apply for a student residence permit at the Immigration Office
below
no later than 2 months before the visa becomes invalid.
Accommodation/housing/room search
You do NOT have an automatic room reservation with your admission to studies.
You must search for your accomodation yourself; the University cannot help you with this.
You will need a permanent address to register at the City Registration Office and to activate your bank account. Start searching at least three months before arriving.
The housing situation in Jena is very difficult in autumns/winter!
Option 1: Apply for a room in the dormitory of the Studierendenwerk Thüringen
Apply for a
furnished room
in one of the
halls of residence
External link
in any case, even if you have not received your admission letter yet.
Apply
External link
by 15 January or 15 July.
Make sure you remember to confirm your application and subsequent offer by e-mail, too
. If you get an offer, please accept it, there will be no second offer, don't be picky. If finally you do not want to take the room, you can reject the offer before lectures start.
Places are few and there is a high demand, therefore there is no guarantee you will be given a place in the halls of residence. Therefore, please also read the information about searching for private rental offers:
Option 2: Private rental, apartments, shared flats
Please be aware that it can be extremely difficult to find a private accommodation in Jena and that, if you are successful, it might be rather expensive. We therefore recommend that, from the start, you also look for accommodation in
neighbouring cities
(e.g. Weimar, Erfurt, Kahla, Gera, Apolda, Camburg, Stadtroda, Rudolstadt, Saalfeld) to where you can commute for free with your semester ticket. Many of our students commute every day. A train ride from Weimar takes about 15 minutes, from Erfurt 25-30 minutes only.

All non-EU citizens will usually have to prove their financial resources with a blocked account when applying for a visa or residence permit.

Deadlines: enrolment & arrival, semester dates, help & contact
Dates and important deadlines:
The
summer semester
2026 begins on 1 April 2026 and will end on 30 September 2026. Lectures start on 7 April 2026 and finish on 10 July 2026. Enrolment ended on 17 April 2026.
The
winter semester
2026/27 begins on 1 October 2026 and will end on 31 March 2027. Lectures start on 19 October 2026 and finish on 12 February 2027. Enrolment ends on 30 October 2026.
Note
: Saturday, 3 October 2026, is a public holiday; public institutions like the University and all shops are closed.
The
Study Orientation Days
(STET) take place between 1-16 October 2026.
The timeline will help you planning:
winter semester 2026/27
pdf, 103 kb
· de
.
The best time to enrol
is by 30 September 2026, as this will ensure you can take part in the orientation days and the automatic course allocation process in good time. See chapter 2,
Study Orientation Days
.
DSH course participants
please start your enrolment only after the results of the entrance test have been published on 30 September 2026 and by 2 October 2026. Please note the special instructions you will receive after admission and at the entrance test.
Guest students:
make sure you comply with your grant issuer's requirements of the period of stay. Please arrive no later than 1/2 October 2026.
Why the dates are important:
Only
after your enrolment
you will receive your
PIN for the self-registration for the digital campus services
(user account,
below
). This is technically possible on the following day only. You will need this login to register for courses in the Friedolin portal (= building your time table; see chapter 2,
STET
) and for activating your
semester ticket
.
What happens if you miss these dates:
If you do not enrol until after 14 October 2026, you will not be guaranteed a place on courses with limited capacity. However, you can still register for courses once you have successfully completed the enrolment process (this does NOT apply to German courses at the Language Centre or the DSH course!). Admission to study courses is granted indivdually by the respective teachers.
If you arrive after 16 October 2026, the University cannot offer you the full welcome service such as the WelcomeCafé, Welcome Buddy support, special office hours, etc. Also, it is not possible to get a dormitory room during the semester. The search for housing on teh private market is very difficult and the Univerity cannot, unfortuntaley, assist you in this.
Enrolment ends on 30 October 2026, 12:00 noon, definitively,
as the University cannot guarantee the regular study period after this any more. This deadline is set in the
Immatrikulationsordnung
(Enrolment Regulations) of the University and is not subject to negotiations.
If you enrol by 30 October 2026, but wish to arrive later,
there is no guarantee that you can be integrated at all in the current semester cycle. Even though the University might – as an exception from the rule – tolerate late arrival, it may happen that you will not get a place in all courses or be allowed to take exams due to missed classes. This means you may not be able to finish the semester/yaer successfully and will likely have to extend your study period for 1-2 semesters. This may lead to problems later rearding the extension of residence permts and financing your studies. You must wage this personal risk. We recommend that you ask for advice from the study programme specific advisory persons. In any case, you are responsible for the organization of your studies and thus also for possible delays and ensuing difficulties.

2. Semester fee payment
All students of the University of Jena have to pay the
semester fee
. This is not a tuition fee. The semester fee for new students includes
the fee for the Studierendenwerk Thüringen,
the semester ticket for the public regional transport in Germany,
the culture ticket,
the contribution for the student council and
plus the Thoska fee €20 (first semester only).
WHEN SHOULD I PAY?
Please pay only
after you arrive in Germany, or when your timely arrival is sure
.
DSH course participants after passing the entrance test.
HOW CAN I PAY?
Sorry, no cash
payment is offered. You have two other options for payment:
OPTION 1 = Card payment - the quick and easy method (5 minutes)
Where? - at the International Office during the
office hours
How? - with MasterCard, Visa, Visa Electron, VPay, EC debit/giro card, Apple/Google Pay (mobile phone). If you have not got such a card yourself, you may also ask a friend who has one to help you.
Bring with you: card/phone, card PIN and passport/personal ID. Keep the payment proof for yourself.
OPTION 2 = Bank transfer - the slower method (up to 1 week)
Why is it slower? - The bank transfer and allocation of your money to your student account will take up to one week.
When? - Please transfer the money after arrival in Jena only or when your timely arrival is sure. After enrolment, no reimbursement.
From which account? -
German or SEPA bank account
(you may use a friends'; note the information about opening a bank account
below.
). Other international transfers: fees apply.
To allocate your payment, the University might ask for a bank transfer statement
in German or English
which must contain the
sum, reference code, university IBAN, booking date, name of the account holder and his/her IBAN
.
For the winter semester 2026/27 please transfer
353.05 €
to this account:

City residents' registration office
Within 14 days after entering the country (or at the next available date), you should register your residential address at the Citizens' Service Centre of your place of residence. To do this, you will need a housing provider certificate, which you will receive from your landlord.
In Jena, you must book an
appointment online
External link
. If you live in another city, please ask your housing provider where to register.
Note: it is
not
necessary to hand in your registration certificate for enrolment.
Bank account
For recurring payments like rent, health insurance, mobile phone/internet, broadcasting fee (see point 4 below) and much more you need an account.
If you are an
EU citizen
and have an account in the EU (SEPA), you can use it.
Please see our information about regular and blocked accounts in our website on
financing your studies
.
Immigration Office: student residence permit
Non-EU citizens whose entry visa is shorter than the planned stay must apply for a residence title for the purpose of studying at the latest 2 months before the expiry of the entry visa.
Non-EU citizens who were able to enter without a visa apply for a residence title for the purpose of studying no later than 6 weeks after entry.
You may print student certificates (valid without stamp and signature) for the Immigration Office from
Friedolin 2.0
External link
.
Applying for a residence permit at the Immigration Office is possible only 2-3 working days after registering your address at the City Resident's Registration Office.
If you live in Jena, send your documents for applying for a residence title to the Aliens' Registration Office of the City of Jena.
Further information
External link
.
If you do not live in Jena, ask your registration office (Bürgerservice/ Einwohnermeldeamt) where your Aliens' Registration Office is located and how to register there.
If your appointment for collecting your residence permit is after your visa/old permit becomes invalid and before your leave Jena, request an earlier appointment by email.
Broadcasting licence fees
Every household has to pay the broadcasting licence fee, known as the Rundfunkbeitrag (previously GEZ), even if there is no television, radio or internet. The good news is that people living in a shared flat can divide the fee amongst the occupants. Watching television and listening to the radio are good ways to learn German. There are really great broadcasts. You can find more information on the licence fee
